summary: Learn workforce planning for AI and automation with scenarios, skills gaps, role maps, and dashboards. Build a transition plan you can use immediately.
lede: Workforce planning for AI and automation transition provides a structured way to connect automation roadmaps and business strategy with roles, skills, headcount, and capability development. The course helps you assess current workforce capacity, anticipate future skill demand, and make staffing and reskilling decisions using evidence rather than assumption. You will build practical tools including a skills gap matrix, future-state role map, transition roadmap, workforce risk register, scenario-based staffing model, and executive-ready reporting pack. You will also explore role segmentation, skills taxonomies, capacity modeling, AI-assisted skills inference, HR analytics dashboards, and automation impact mapping while working with imperfect data and competing priorities.
audienceIntro: This course is built for professionals who need to translate AI and automation plans into realistic workforce actions. You will work with role maps, skills gaps, scenario models, and transition roadmaps that fit day-to-day operational decision-making. Workforce Planners who model demand, supply, and role transitions. HR Business Partners who support automation-related people decisions. Talent Strategists who define skills priorities and reskilling pathways. Organization Development Specialists who redesign roles and job families. Transformation Managers who align staffing plans with automation roadmaps. HR Analytics Specialists who build workforce dashboards and gap reports. Learning and Development Managers who target upskilling to future roles. Compensation and Job Architecture Specialists who update role structures. Change Managers who manage communication around role redesign and automation. People Operations Leads who coordinate workforce transition actions across functions.
prerequisites: Participants should have working knowledge of HR, talent, workforce planning, or transformation processes. Familiarity with basic HR metrics, role profiles, and organizational structure is helpful. No coding is required, but you should be comfortable reviewing spreadsheets, dashboards, and scenario models. Advanced concepts such as AI-assisted skills analysis will be taught at an operational application level, not as technical engineering.
